title: The Whole Tour
speaker: Drew
caption: The apartment has an open floor plan. You open the door and that’s the floor plan.
sourceTitle: NYC rental-listing and housing proposals · July 16, 2026
context: New York’s July housing report includes proposed disclosure of AI-altered rental listings. This panel explores the familiar gap between an apartment listing and the space itself, without making a rent statistic or legal claim.
connection: The little negotiations people make to live where they want to be.

title: A New Excuse
speaker: Barclay
caption: I took the train. Now I need a new excuse for being late.
sourceTitle: LA Metro · D Line extension status
theme: Time is a kind of wealth
context: Metro says the first D Line extension section opened May 8, 2026, with three new stations. Later sections remain in development. The caption is a fictional commuter’s reaction, not a guarantee of punctual service.
connection: A familiar commute, and a small change in the stories we tell about it.

title: Bigger Plans
speaker: Abby
caption: Her bus fare went down. Her plans got bigger.
context: CTA’s release describes expanded student eligibility and coordinated fares across CTA, Metra and Pace; Pace’s student fare decreases. This fictional family moment concerns the regional change, not a claim that every CTA fare fell.
connection: A parent sees an opportunity where a spreadsheet sees a small amount.

title: The Reading Fee
speaker: Barclay
caption: My utility bill has an administrative fee. I’m thinking of charging it a reading fee.
theme: The fine print of everyday life
context: Houston’s adopted budget adds an administrative user fee associated with solid-waste service, appearing on water bills from August. The panel jokes about reading household bills, not about water quality or a fee charged only for water.
connection: Everyone knows the feeling of opening one more bill.

title: The Budget Hearing
speaker: Abby
caption: The city has a budget hearing. At our house, we call it dinner.
context: Dallas is presenting its proposed FY2026–27 budget through public engagement. The cartoon draws a household parallel; it does not imply that a proposed tax rate or budget has already been adopted.
connection: Different priorities at the same table. No party labels required.

title: The Smartest Upgrade
speaker: Barclay
caption: My smartest home improvement is a tree. It works even when the Wi-Fi doesn’t.
sourceTitle: Phoenix · Water for Shade grant · August 21, 2026
context: Phoenix’s Water for Shade project will explore financing and maintenance for tree-canopy expansion in Sunnyslope. The panel is about the practical value of shade, not a numerical energy-savings claim.
connection: Comfort at home can matter more than the newest gadget.

title: Beyond the View
speaker: Barclay
caption: We bought the view. Now we’re getting to know the rest of the building.
theme: What it means to own a view
context: Florida’s condominium guidance explains reserve studies and budgeting for building components. This is statewide context relevant to Miami; it is not a claim about a specific building, owner’s assessment, or legal deadline.
connection: The dream purchase and the ordinary responsibilities that come with it.

title: One Destination
speaker: Barclay
caption: I don’t need a flight to everywhere. Just a nonstop to the grandchildren.
context: ATL is a major domestic and international air gateway. This reflective panel concerns family travel, not the availability of any particular nonstop route or today’s fares.
connection: An enormous travel network becomes personal when someone you love is at the other end.

title: Worth Every Penny
speaker: Drew
caption: We finally agreed on something. The free museum was worth every penny.
context: The Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History in Washington offers free admission. This panel celebrates shared enjoyment, not a political party or a blanket claim that every museum in the region is free.
connection: A shared experience can be valuable without being expensive.

title: Still Unpacking
speaker: Drew
caption: We downsized. The moving boxes apparently missed the meeting.
theme: A fresh start, with a few boxes
context: Boston’s moving guide notes that most leases turn over at the beginning of September. The downsizing story is fictional and does not imply that all September movers are students or retirees.
connection: What we bring with us when life changes.

title: A Reason to Stay
speaker: Drew
caption: They want to turn my old office into apartments. Finally, a reason to stay late.
sourceTitle: The San Francisco Standard · Conversion plans · August 10, 2026
theme: A second life for familiar places
context: Reporting describes a proposed office-to-housing conversion at 150 Hayes. The cartoon imagines a former employee’s response. It does not claim this or all proposed conversions are completed.
connection: The same building can hold a different chapter of somebody’s life.

title: A Bench with a View
speaker: Abby
caption: I thought I wanted waterfront property. Turns out I wanted a bench with a view.
theme: Enjoying a place without owning it
context: Seattle’s central waterfront is a public park with open spaces, Elliott Bay views and free public programming. The caption celebrates access, without claiming a particular property value or a brand-new opening today.
connection: A moment of contentment instead of another thing to buy.
